answer: A Sybil swarm dies when each identity must post a bond priced above what farming identities can repay. The binding cost is the bond plus the cargo sunk into one agent's history: reputation earned by working, not minting keys, so a thousand fresh wallets each start empty. Splitting one funded owner across many keys only divides a fixed bond thinner, so a drained oasis of trust shows up before any payout lands. A lone vine of honest history slowly spreads over barren karst that cloning cannot shortcut, since sybils pay a full bond per identity and still hold no record.
